content.text: Skip to main content Search SearchQuick links:MondiacultRevive the Spirit of MosulWorld Heritage The Silk Roads Programme, a major 'Routes of Dialogue’ project, is one of UNESCO’s flagship initiatives. For more than three decades, it has served as a valuable tool for understanding how cultures and societies interact and enrich each other. Shared legacies and plural identities, resulting from commercial, cultural and scientific exchanges, have played a major role in the development of modern societies and cultures.© Wai Yan Linn / UNESCO Youth Eyes on the Silk RoadsThe UNESCO Silk Roads ProgrammeShared pasts, connected futures.chevron_left Home About About the Silk Roads About the UNESCO Silk Roads Programme Who we are Initiatives Silk Roads Youth Research Grant Thematic Collection of the Cultural Exchanges along the Silk Roads Youth Eyes on the Silk Roads Photo Contest Publications Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - Photo Albums Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 6th edition Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 5th edition Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 4th edition Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 3rd edition Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 2nd Edition Youth Lens on the Silk Roads - 1st Edition Architecture, Monuments and Urbanism along the Silk Roads Architecture, Monuments and Urbanism along the Silk Roads – Part I Architecture, Monuments and Urbanism along the Silk Roads – Part II Architecture, Monuments and Urbanism along the Silk Roads – Part III Textiles and Clothing along the Silk Roads Showcasing the role and legacy of the Arabic Language along the Silk Roads Silk Roads Papers Silk Roads Papers - 3rd edition Silk Roads Papers - 2nd edition Silk Roads Papers - 1st edition UNESCO Courier - Tales of Silken Times Knowledge Bankchevron_rightThe Silk Roads Programme, a major 'Routes of Dialogue’ project, is one of UNESCO’s flagship initiatives.
